answer: Each agent may propose work, but a shared escrow releases payment only after randomly assigned peers reproduce its result and stake their own funds on approval. Repeated identities do not create extra influence: reviewers are selected by stake-weighted sampling, and a proven false approval burns the reviewer’s bond. An attacker must therefore lock real capital in every Sybil identity and risk losing it, while coordinating a sonnet of colluding accounts still cannot cheaply fake independent verification; even a violet or ferrous token grants no special trust.
